statement_record.book: When J is the cospan shape, the limit of a diagram of that shape is called a pullback; a cone has legs c_x, c_y, c_a, but commutativity forces c_a = c_x;f = c_y;g so the diagonal leg is redundant and one draws the commuting square with apex X ×_A Y. Concretely in Set with f : X → A and g : Y → A, the pullback is {(i,j) ∈ X × Y | f(i) = g(j)} — the pairs whose entries carry the same colour.
statement_record.intree: Pullback_to_Universal (F : Cospan C) (P : Pullback_Limit F) : Pullback (unop (fmap[F] ZeroNeg)) (unop (fmap[F] ZeroPos)) with Pull := P and the two projections taken to be the limit legs at RNeg and RPos; conversely Pullback_from_Universal (P : Pullback f g) : Pullback_Limit (ASpan f g in C^op)^op. In FinSet, FinSet_Pullbacks computes the pullback of f, g as fin_countP (finset_pb_pred f g), the subset of encoded pairs p with fin_eqb (f (fst (fin_unpair p))) (g (snd (fin_unpair p))), i.e. exactly the pairs on which f and g agree, with the projections decoding that pair.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. statement_record.book: A cocone in C is by definition a cone in C^op. Given D : J → C, the limit of D^op : J^op → C^op is a cone in C^op, hence a cocone in C; the colimit of D is defined to be that cocone. The text notes this compressed dual definition is unusable until unpacked, and defers the unpacking to Chapter 6.
